rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when an idea, attempt, or situation is absurdly unreasonable or over the top.

example.english: You say you can make an elevator out of cardboard boxes? That’s ludicrous.
example.traditional: 你話用紙皮箱整升降機，真係離譜喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 waa6 jung6 zi2 pei4 soeng1 zing2 sing1 gong3 gei1 zan1 hai6 lei4 pou2 wo3

rows.note: Use this for a more precise description of something plainly absurd or logically unthinkable, rather than merely excessive.

example.english: This line of reasoning is completely ludicrous; how can you say he’s guilty without any evidence?
example.traditional: 呢個推理完全荒謬，點可能冇證據就話佢有罪？
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 teoi1 lei5 jyun4 cyun4 fong1 mau6 dim2 ho2 nang4 mou5 zing3 geoi3 zau6 waa6 keoi5 jau5 zeoi6

rows.note: Use this colloquially when the ludicrous thing seems idiotic or crazy, especially in an emphatic reaction.

example.english: Taking a taxi to the next street just to save one dollar is ludicrous, isn’t it?
example.traditional: 為咗慳一蚊搭的士去隔籬街，痴線㗎？
example.jyutping: wai6 zo2 haan1 jat1 man1 daap3 dik1 si2 heoi3 gaak3 lei4 gaai1 ci1 sin3 gaa3
